subject: Request: LLM training/data retention & DPIA for FinHealth pilot
messages:
From: Amelia Ruiz <dpo@finhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@finhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial questions: LLM training on customer data / DPIA

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As FinHealth prepares a small pilot using Redwood's hosted API for several PII-bearing use cases, our Data Protection Office needs to confirm a few things before the pilot starts.

High-level questions:
- Do you ever use customer-provided prompts or responses to further train or fine-tune Redwood models (either hosted or dedicated customers)? If yes, please describe opt-out mechanisms and timelines.
- For hosted API traffic: what parts of requests/responses are logged, for how long, and who can access logs? Please include retention windows and whether prompts/responses are used for improvement/quality training.
- Can you provide a brief DPIA outline or template showing potential risks and mitigations for an LLM integration (data flows, categories of data processed, lawful basis mapping)?
- We also need SOC 2 evidence sections that cover model training/usage and data handling, plus a data flow diagram that shows where tokens, KV cache or prompts are persisted.

If you can send a short summary and any standard documents we can share with our legal/compliance team, that would be ideal. We're on a tight timeline to kick off the pilot in two weeks.

Best,
Amelia Ruiz
DPO, FinHealth Inc.

(attachment: finhealth_dpo_questions.xlsx)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ruiz <dpo@finhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions: LLM training on customer data / DPIA

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear list. We're fully prepared to support a DPIA and provide the SOC 2 excerpts. Short answers up front:

- Training on customer data: Redwood does not use customer prompts/responses to continue training or retrain public models by default. Hosted customers may opt-in to share telemetry for aggregated product improvements; default is opt-out. Dedicated/Private deployments never feed customer data back into model training.
- Logs & retention: For hosted API, request/response logs are retained by default for 30 days for debugging and abuse detection; configurable down to 0 days for customers on Dedicated/Private or by contract. Access is role-based (SRE/support with audited access). We can provide retention SLAs in the DPA.
- DPIA: attaching a short DPIA summary and our standard data flow PNG. We'll also attach the SOC 2 excerpt that references data handling for inference telemetry.

I'll follow up with a short internal checklist and loop in Rishi and Monica to produce a tailored DPIA/cover memo for FinHealth.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpia_summary_v1.pdf; data_flow_diagram.png; SOC2-llm-section.txt

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Initial questions: LLM training on customer data / DPIA

Team — forwarding FinHealth's DPO questions. They need answers and a short DPIA memo by COB on Thu to keep their pilot timeline. Key asks to address in the memo:

1) Explicit statement on training: confirm hosted default is no training on customer prompts/responses; document opt-in telemetry program and how customers can opt-out (API flag & Console toggle). Include examples and dates when the opt-in was introduced.
2) Data retention and access: provide tables of what we store (request metadata, full prompts, model responses, KV-cache pointers), default retention periods, and how Dedicated/Private customers can change retention or disable storage entirely. Note ACLs and audited access paths.
3) Data flows & DPIA mitigations: map categories (personal data, health data), describe lawful basis we recommend (contractual necessity/legitimate interest with DPIA evidence), and mitigations (encryption at rest/in transit, tokenization, field-level redaction suggestions, privacy-preserving logging).
4) Evidence: pull the SOC 2 excerpt that references telemetry and access controls; include the data flow PNG and a brief section on how on-prem / VPC deployments avoid telemetry leakage.

Rishi — can you draft the retention/access table and confirm the console toggle names and API param for opt-out? Monica — please draft the DPIA memo and a short customer-facing blurb we can send to Amelia with pointers to contractual language (DPA & SCCs). Put drafts in the FinHealth Drive folder linked below.

Thanks,
Neha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ruiz <dpo@finhealth.com>
Cc: legal@finhealth.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions: LLM training on customer data / DPIA — FinHealth pilot

Hi Amelia,

Thanks again for the patience — attached are the materials your team requested for the pilot:
- redwood_dpia_summary_v1.pdf — concise DPIA outline (risks, likelihood, mitigation, residual risk)
- data_flow_diagram.png — shows flow for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments
- SOC2-llm-section.txt — excerpt describing telemetry handling, access controls, and auditing

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Training on customer data: Redwood's default policy for hosted customers is not to use customer prompts/responses to train or fine-tune models. We operate a separate opt-in telemetry program (customers may enable "improve_model" in Console or set improve_model=true on the API) if they want their anonymized prompts/responses used for aggregated model improvements. That program has explicit consent, documented retention, and customers can opt-out at any time. Dedicated and Private customers' data is never included in opt-in telemetry by default.

- Retention & access: By default hosted logs (request metadata and full prompts/responses for debugging) are retained 30 days. Customers on Dedicated can set retention to 0 (no storage) or a custom value via contract. Access to logs is strictly role-based and audited; support must request access and it's logged in the audit trail. See redwood_dpia_summary_v1.pdf for table with fields retained and retention windows.

- DPIA & lawful basis: The DPIA summary maps categories that FinHealth flagged (health/PII) and recommends contractual necessity as the lawful basis for processing under GDPR for the pilot. We include mitigations like tokenization, field redaction, and application-level pseudonymization. See attached for details.

- Evidence & next steps: Attached SOC2 excerpt covers telemetry controls; the data flow PNG shows where KV cache and temporary storage exist and how they are isolated per-tenant. If you need a tailored DPA amendment or SCCs bundled, our legal team can prepare a short addendum — propose we set a call with your legal on Friday if helpful.

If you want, we can also supply a short sandbox configuration that disables request/response retention and routes logs to your VPC for the pilot.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Compliance
Redwood Inference
